Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As part of our RFP security review we'd like to confirm a few items in the vulnerability management section of the questionnaire you returned. Can you provide the following: 1) SBOM in CycloneDX or SPDX for the hosted API; 2) high-level summary of the most recent external penetration test (date, vendor, severity breakdown and remediation status); 3) your patching SLA commitments for critical/high/medium findings affecting the hosted control plane and model-serving runtime; and 4) brief description of SAST/DAST cadence and tooling you use (and whether results are gated on deploy).

We're on a tight timeline for the procurement committee; if you can share artifacts or an internal point of contact who can coordinate delivery that would be helpful.

Best,

Eleanor,

Appreciate the clear list — we can get everything over to you. Attaching a preliminary set of answers to the questionnaire and a short process overview for our SAST/DAST/patching practices.

Quick answers up front:
- SBOM: yes, we can provide CycloneDX and SPDX exports; preliminary CycloneDX attached.
- Pen test: external test performed Q2 2026 by BlueHarbor Security; summary attached (no critical findings; three medium findings closed 2026-07-15).
- Patch SLA (hosted Redwood API / runtime): Critical (P0) - mitigation within 24 hours and full corrective patch deployment within 72 hours; High (P1) - mitigation or workaround within 48 hours, patch within 7 calendar days; Medium (P2) - next monthly maintenance window (target 30 days); Low - tracked in quarterly backlog. For Dedicated/Private customers we publish advisories and provide upgrade artifacts; hotfix support can be contracted.
- SAST/DAST: We run SAST (static analysis + SCA) on every pull request and a weekly full SCA scan; DAST (dynamic scanning + authenticated tests) is run monthly against staging and during any major release, and we require fail-on-critical in CI for code that touches the runtime.

I'm attaching: vuln_questionnaire_answers.xlsx, redwood_sbom_2026-07-cyclonedx.xml (CycloneDX), pen_test_summary_q2_2026.pdf, and a short SAST/DAST process doc. Vivek and Marissa are looped in for procurement terms and to confirm any additional evidence you need.

If you need a signed attestation or SOC2 evidence, we can route that through our security/compliance team — would you like that now or on the committee cadence?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Sales
Redwood Inference

Neha,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments — we reviewed the summary. A couple of follow-ups before we proceed to scoring:

1) SBOM: We need the CycloneDX at component granularity (including direct and transitive deps) and a sha256 for each artifact. The XML you shared looks promising but please confirm it covers the hosted runtime images (model-serving runtime) and the console.

2) Pen test deliverable: please confirm whether the pen-test PDF includes evidence of remediation and dates for each closed finding. We typically require a remediation verification (re-test) or compensating control for medium findings.

3) Patch SLA: Your SLA statement is good for hosted. Please confirm if SLAs differ for Dedicated nodes and for on-prem/private installs (we expect different behavior there). Also: what is your published definition of "mitigation" vs "patch deployment"?

4) Evidence of gating: does your CI/CD pipeline block merges on critical SAST findings? If not, what compensating controls exist?

If you can send an updated CycloneDX with SHA256s and a pen-test appendix that references remediation verification (or a timeline to complete any outstanding items) by EOD Friday we can include Redwood in the initial short-list.

Regards,
StraitBridge Security Ops

Eleanor / Security Ops team,

Thanks for the follow-ups — sending the updated package attached. Summary of what we included and answers to your clarifying points below.

Attachments in this message: redwood_sbom_2026-07-cyclonedx.xml (CycloneDX, includes sha256 for each listed component), pen_test_summary_q2_2026.pdf (appendix added with remediation verification dates), vuln_questionnaire_answers.xlsx (updated), sast_dast_process_overview.docx.

SBOM scope: The CycloneDX export covers the hosted API control plane, model-serving runtime container images used in our hosted fleet, and the Redwood Console. For Dedicated and Private customers we provide the same CycloneDX export for the artifacts we ship; for on-prem installs customers can run the same SBOM generator locally — we provide the tooling.

Pen test summary (BlueHarbor Security, 2026-06-22):
- Engagement: external black-box + authenticated tests against staging and pre-prod control plane.
- Severity breakdown: 0 Critical, 1 High, 3 Medium, 6 Low.
- Remediation: High finding (privilege escalation via misconfigured container capability) mitigated 2026-06-29 with a configuration rollback and kernel capability restriction; permanent patch deployed 2026-07-10. The three medium findings were closed 2026-07-15 after code fixes and config hardening; re-test verification for those items performed 2026-07-20 (see appendix in PDF).

Patch SLA clarifications (hosted vs Dedicated/Private):
- Hosted (Redwood-managed):
  - Critical (P0): Temporary mitigation in 24 hours (e.g., traffic routing, feature toggle, WAF rule), full patch deployment to fleet within 72 hours.
  - High (P1): Mitigation/workaround within 48 hours, patch deployment within 7 calendar days.
  - Medium (P2): Target next monthly maintenance window (target 30 days).
  - Low (P3): Planned in next quarterly backlog.
- Dedicated & Private (customer-managed runtime images or air-gapped installs):
  - We publish advisories, hotfix packages, and upgrade scripts within 24 hours of a public CVE (if exploitability confirmed). SLA for patch deployment depends on contracted managed services; default is advisory + hotfix within 7 days; we offer paid expedited remediation assistance.

Definition: 'Mitigation' = action that materially reduces or removes customer exposure (network-level rule, feature disable, temporary config change). 'Patch deployment' = code or configuration update applied to runtime images and rolled out to production fleet following our rollout policy (can include canary + auto-fallback).

SAST/DAST gating and controls:
- SAST: We run static analysis on every pull request using multiple scanners (OSS + commercial engines). The pipeline blocks merges on findings classified as "Critical" and treats "High" as hard warn in most components (configurable by team). For our runtime and control plane modules we enforce block-on-High for any code that touches privileged container startup paths.
- DAST: Dynamic scans run in staging and are part of the release checklist. Fail-on-critical is enforced during release promotion; compensating controls are required for any non-blocking findings (detailed in the attached process doc).

Additional notes:
- For SOC2 or signed attestations please let me know and I will route to our compliance team — we can provide SOC2 Type II reports (redacted) under an NDA.
- If you want a short walk-through of the pen test appendix and live remediation timeline we can schedule a 30-minute call with our Head of Security.

Next steps: please confirm if the attached artifacts satisfy your procurement panel. If you need any additional hashes, provenance metadata, or CI evidence (e.g., pipeline logs showing gating events) we can extract those as follow-up items.

Regards,
